maria: quick postmortem from today's AWQ bakeoff — summary first: AWQ (4-bit weights + act-quant) with group_size=64 gave best offline perplexity on our validation suite (delta -0.9 vs FP16) but in serving we hit intermittent instability: token dropouts and occasional NaNs in softmax. rolling back to GPTQ/INT8 avoids it.

sam: ugh. any logs? naive hunch: act-quant scaling mismatch or group boundary handling when kv-cache merges.

maria: pasted snippet from runtime logs on canary (hosted-dedicated):
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] WARNING runtime: token_gen failed: logits contain NaN
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] INFO fallback: switching model -> gptq-v1 (reason: nan)
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] DEBUG awq: group_size=64 act_quant=4 per_channel_scale=True
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] DEBUG kvcache: merge_seq=2 last_seq=1
```

lee: can you repro locally with the same seed/inputs? AWQ's per-group scale can be sensitive to sequence length and micro-batching. also check act-quant config: do you use symmetric or asymmetric scaling?

maria: symmetric by default. repro script attached (ran on a4x): `python scripts/serve_repro.py --model=awq-qlora-13b --quant=awq --gs=64 --seed=42 --input-file=./repro/edgecases.txt`

ci-bot: test run failed: 1 flaky failure out of 20 (reproducer: ./repro/edgecases.txt), exit_code=2, traceback shows NaN in softmax layer.

jon: two quick experiments: 1) drop group_size -> 32, 2) disable act-quant (keep weights AWQ only). which gives better stability? also try act-ordering=(relu-first) — we had an issue where fused ordering produced overflows.

maria: ran both. results:
- gs=64 actq=on -> 4/20 failures (observed token gaps, NaNs)
- gs=32 actq=on -> 1/20 failures (slightly better)
- gs=64 actq=off -> 0/20 failures but perplexity +1.4 vs best AWQ
- gptq-int8 -> 0/20 failures, perplexity +0.7 vs AWQ best
(benchmarks: LAMBADA acc, MMLU macro, internal convo-eval)

sam: looks like act-quant is the unstable factor. you might try per-tensor act scales instead of per-channel — reduces dynamic range variance. also try clipping activations at runtime (e.g., max_norm=16) as a mitigation.

lee: FYI we saw a similar pattern last quarter with FP8 kernels: loose scaling on per-group caused softmax overflow at long history lengths. patch we used: when merge_seq>1, recompute prefix scales with historical max and clamp. could be applied here.

maria: created a dev branch `awq/stability-repro` with a quick clamp: `act_scale = min(act_scale, historical_max_scale)` and a canary of 10% traffic. deploying now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary=10% -> hosts [ded-04,ded-11], rev=awq/stability-repro@g7f3a, timestamp=1759204380

ci-bot: canary smoke tests: 200/200 for short prompts, fail reproduced on long-history test (seq_len 2048) 1/50.

jon: if canary still flakes after clamp, plan B = automatic fallback policy in routing: route requests with history>1024 to gptq variant. we can add this policy in the routing config quickly.

maria: agreed. next steps: (1) try per-tensor act scale and larger clamp window, (2) run long-history sweep (512/1024/2048) with gs in {32,48,64}, (3) add routing rule for history>1024 -> gptq. i'll own. tagging @sam for eval matrices and @lee for runtime patch review.

sam: happy to produce the eval matrix. will include MMLU, LAMBADA, code-synth, and our convo-eval. will compute delta vs FP16 and GPTQ, include p95 latency and failure rate.

lee: will review patch and run unit tests on kv-cache merge. good catch.

maria: thanks all. I'll update thread with numbers once sweeps finish. :thumbsup:
